policy_title: Increase funding for children's social care
stated: Provide an additional £3bn to local authorities for high-quality children's social care, including consistent access to counsellors for children in foster care or adopted, and extend staying put arrangements for fostered young people until 21.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for an additional £3bn to be provided to local authorities to enable them to provide high-quality children’s social care. Elected Greens will also push for children in foster care or who have been adopted to have consistent access to a trained counsellor until it is no longer required. We would fund councils to extend staying put arrangements, so fostered young people can choose to stay with foster parents until they are 21.

bearing_set.reason: Policy explicitly funds counsellors for looked-after and adopted children, directly addressing mental health access for a high-need, under-served group — a named O3 indicator.

£3bn for children's social care expands local authority capacity to identify and protect children from abuse and neglect — a core child-safety/safeguarding function that materially affects the safety of one of the most vulnerable groups.

Looked-after children have markedly worse attainment; extending staying-put arrangements to age 21 (stability mechanism) and mental health support (engagement mechanism) both plausibly move the attainment gap indicator for this high-deprivation group.

£3bn in additional local authority spending is a material fiscal commitment; no funding source is stated, so it plausibly widens the funded/borrowed gap and bears on the debt-path sustainability indicator.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: opportunity/attainment for care-experienced children (O7), mental health access (O3), and fiscal sustainability of an unstated-funding £3bn pledge (O12). Staying put at 21 is a youth welfare measure, not a pensioner/elderly care measure, so O8 does not apply.
